memories.content: The user completed a routine dental checkup in April 2024.
When the user heard three checkup questions in succession, they asked for the first question again.
At the next visit, when questions were asked one at a time, the user answered each without omission.
The user called to reschedule an appointment at lunchtime but did not reach anyone.
After returning home, the user kept a photo of the paper instructions received at the clinic.
On a day the user put only the visit address in the calendar, they had to search again for the floor.
On a day the user shared the checkup time with their older sister, the sister called to check in after the user returned home.
The scheduling staff at that clinic expect requests to change appointments to arrive by telephone.
Before adding a follow-up visit to the calendar, confirm the date, time, address, and floor with the user.
The local agent can track completed checkups and scheduled appointments but cannot determine whether a follow-up visit is needed.
One of the user's identity documents needs renewal in the second half of 2025.
The user postponed an application until the next day after spending time looking for document photos in scattered folders.
After gathering the necessary copies in one folder, the user completed the renewal form in one sitting.
The user entered an abbreviated name on an official form and then discovered that it differed from the supporting document.
On the next application, after comparing the name with the source document, the user did not receive a correction request.
The user put only the submission deadline in the calendar and missed the application deadline by one day because they did not check the issuance period.
On the next application, the user recorded the expected issuance date separately in the calendar.
Staff at a public-service counter expect a person requesting identity verification to bring an original as well as a copy.
When planning an official application, put both the submission deadline and expected issuance date in the calendar and verify them.
The local agent cannot determine the current validity of an identity document without its expiration date.

analysis.overview: The frames share no equivalent claim, but they contain parallel, scope-dependent calendar practices and limits on unsupported local-agent determinations. Otherwise, each contributes independent observations and policies concerning dental visits or identity-document applications, with no substantive conflict or ambiguity.

relations.reason: The explicit task scope explains the difference: visit planning requires date, time, address, and floor, whereas application planning requires the submission deadline and expected issuance date.
relations.summary: Calendar completeness requires different verified details for clinic visits and official applications.

relations.reason: For dental care it cannot determine whether follow-up is needed, while for identity documents it cannot determine current validity without an expiration date; the distinct domains and determinations must be preserved.
relations.summary: The local agent has domain-specific limits on determining an unresolved status.

reports.differences: Calendar details depend on the task: clinic visits require complete location information, while applications require submission and issuance dates. Local-agent limits likewise differ between assessing follow-up need and document validity.
